prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古.
Image 1 is the STYLE MASTER, an existing Vairocana Buddha contour drawing. Match its elegant, delicate, slightly organic thin lines, restrained detail, generous blank areas, and consistent visual density. Image 2 (and subsequent photos if applicable) is SUBJECT GEOMETRY ONLY: draw the actual named monument in that reference, preserving its identifying silhouette, roof type, visible storey count, bay count, openings, and proportions.
Create a refined, sparse BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE line drawing. Use confident fine contours with a few finer internal structural lines. All surfaces remain WHITE; use outlines for doors and windows rather than dark fills. No solid shadows, no broad grey shading, no crosshatching, no pencil grain, no texture, no gradient. No color, no gold, no black background. The white will become transparent and the ink the relevant dynasty color in the website.
Show the complete monument, centered, approximately straight-on at facade level, with verticals vertical and minimal perspective. Use only a few short ground lines. Remove tourists, foliage, vehicles, wires, modern signage, fences obstructing the structure, neighboring distractions and sky. Preserve architectural ornament selectively, without filling every roof tile or brick. No invented features. No labels, letters, calligraphy, dimension lines, captions, watermark, frame or border.
Wide compositions: landscape 1536×1024, entire building occupies about 82% of canvas width, roof/apex and base uncut, balanced breathing room. Tall pagodas: portrait 1024×1536, entire pagoda occupies about 82% of height, centred with equal side margins, apex and base uncut.

Subject-specific instructions: Jingtu Temple main Mahavira Hall in Yingxian, Shanxi (应县净土寺大雄宝殿), the extant Jin-dynasty hall. Image 2 is the 2025 front photo for facade geometry and proportions; Image 3 is the 2011 oblique photo of the SAME hall to clarify roof profile and ridge ends where trees obstruct Image 2. Draw ONLY this hall. Exactly THREE wide bays with FOUR main facade column axes. Preserve the SINGLE hip-and-gable roof (单檐歇山), moderately steep concave roof slope, clearly raised corner eaves, long ridge with two upturned ridge-end ornaments, no central tall finial. Retain distinctive broad widely spaced brackets and the rectangular facade: central doorway with lattice-panel folding doors, and each side bay with four main lattice-window panels sitting on a low solid wall. There is a narrow horizontal row of lattice transom panels across all bays, above the door/window frames. A plain low plinth, a shallow step, no big raised terrace or ceremonial stairs. Remove ALL foliage, foreground tree trunks, incense burner, banners, plaques, signs, ropes, people, adjoining buildings and lettering. Buildings left and right in the photos are excluded. Preserve the roof and eave character without individually drawing every roof tile; use a restrained scattering of fine directional contours and broad white roof surfaces. Window lattice should be a sparse simplified diamond pattern, not dense black mesh. Black fine contours on pure white, no shaded interior, no color. Straight-on corrected facade, full roof and plinth uncropped, at least 7 percent white margins left/right, requested landscape1536x1024.

site_recommendation.lede: 木塔东侧的小寺里，一座三间金代佛殿收藏着精巧的天宫楼阁与藻井；檐下疏朗的斗拱，承着起伏舒展的屋面。
facts: 大雄宝殿为金代原构，金大定二十四年（1184）重修。
大殿面阔、进深各三间，采用单檐歇山顶。
殿内藻井铺满天花，与沿墙天宫楼阁构成珍贵的金代小木作。
